subject: Data region & deployment routing: EU primary, APAC latency needs - next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>, Tomoko Saito <tomoko.saito@apactech.jp>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Data region & deployment routing: EU primary, APAC latency needs - next steps

Hi Elena, Tomoko —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the residency and deployment questions that came up.

Summary of constraints you mentioned:
- EU regulator requires customer data to be stored and processed within the EU for production PHI/PFSI workflows.
- You have an APAC user base that needs sub-200ms regional latency for interactive features (chat).
- Procurement needs a clear list of deployment options and the tradeoffs for security/compliance and cost.

Redwood deployment options mapped to your needs (high level):
1) Hosted API (EU region): fastest to pilot, we can limit processing/storage to EU-hosted clusters and provide SOC2/audit logs. Good for quick time-to-value; cross-region calls from APAC will see higher latency unless we use edge routing or local caching.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved EU pool + optional APAC burst): predictable throughput and isolation. Can add an APAC dedicated pool for low-latency routing, but that increases commit/cost.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full control over data residency and networking; best for strict regulatory requirements. Longer lead time for provisioning and connectivity.

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Can you confirm which of your workloads require strict EU-only processing vs which can tolerate APAC-edge calls? (e.g., admin logs vs customer-facing chat)
- I'll put together a short pilot plan that keeps production EU-bound for regulated flows while testing a local APAC cache for latency-sensitive interactions.
- I'll loop in Redwood Security for a quick check on KMS/HSM integrations.

Attaching the notes I took on requirements (FinServ_EU_requirements.docx) and a preliminary cost worksheet (redwood-deploy-cost-estimate.xlsx).

If it helps, we can do a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week to walk through network/topology options — do you have availability Thu/Fri?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0184

Attachments: FinServ_EU_requirements.docx, redwood-deploy-cost-estimate.xlsx

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tomoko Saito <tomoko.saito@apactech.jp>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 17:36:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Data region & deployment routing: EU primary, APAC latency needs - next steps

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Anything that touches PII or payment data must remain in the EU for processing and storage. That includes our fraud-detection model inputs and historical logs.
- Our customer-facing chat can tolerate eventual consistency for analytics, but not for inference latency — chat must be sub-200ms for APAC users.
- For procurement: we need an explicit list of evidence items (SOC2, data flow diagrams, encryption in transit/at rest, KMS details) and a rough timeline for Private/VPC provisioning if we choose that route.

Action items for Redwood:
- Confirm whether Hosted API (EU-only) can be guaranteed not to route tokens or KV cache lookups via non-EU regions.
- Provide details on Dedicated capacity options that allow APAC-edge routing or burst capacity without replicating regulated data.

Tomoko: can you share approximate APAC user volume for peak hours so Ben can size recommendations?

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform Risk | FinServ EU
Elena.Rossi@finserv-eu.com

Attachment: FinServ_regulatory_summary.pdf (uploaded separately)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finserv-eu.com>, Tomoko Saito <tomoko.saito@apactech.jp>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data region & deployment routing: EU primary, APAC latency needs - next steps

Elena —

Helpful details, thank you. Quick responses inline and a concrete pilot suggestion:  

Inline:
- Hosted API (EU-only) guarantee: Yes — for hosted customers we can pin processing and persistent storage to an EU region and provide a signed data flow diagram and SOC2 artifact. Runtime routing for live traffic can be constrained via our routing policy; KV/cache replication can be disabled for regulated namespaces. I'll share the artifact and routing policy excerpt with Priyom and Vivek.
- Dedicated capacity options: We can provision a dedicated EU pool for regulated inference. For APAC latency-sensitive features we propose one of two approaches:
  a) APAC edge with request-proxy + local prefix cache: inference still happens in EU (for regulated classes) but we keep a prefix/KV cache in APAC to serve hot prompts and reduce round-trip for non-regulated queries. This avoids storing regulated data outside EU.
  b) Secondary APAC dedicated pool with token-masking & filtered sync: we replicate only non-PII embeddings and model parameters necessary for low-latency inference; regulated datasets remain EU-only. This gives best latency but increases cost and operational scope.

Pilot proposal (3 weeks):
Week 0: Agree classification of regulated vs non-regulated flows; sign off on pilot scope.
Week 1: Stand up EU hosted or dedicated instance with strict routing; implement prefix caching in APAC test cluster for chat experiments (non-regulated class).
Week 2: Run traffic mirroring from APAC to test cache; measure latency and cache hit rate.
Deliverable: decision memo with recommended deployment (Hosted-EU + APAC cache vs Dedicated dual-pool) and estimated 12-month cost delta.

I'll attach the routing policy excerpt and a sample data flow artifact for your procurement team. Vivek, can you confirm whether the KMS/HSM integration we offer meets their procurement checklist or if we need an enterprise add-on?

Tomoko — could you share peak qps and user concurrency for your APAC chat so we can spec the cache?

If Thu/Fri works for you, I'll schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive.

Best,
Ben

Subject: Re: Data region & deployment routing: EU primary, APAC latency needs - next steps

Hi team —

Quick security note and next ops tasking:
- Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for Private and Dedicated deployments; hosted customers can use our managed KMS with customer-passphrases. We will provide the KMS integration guide and the HSM options in the packet.
- For EU-only processing: we can disable cross-region KV replication and enforce region-scoped namespaces. That will be part of the deployment runbook.
- For APAC edge caching approach (option a): we need to ensure request-level PII redaction before leaving EU boundaries. We'll prototype a request-filter that strips/obfuscates regulated fields prior to cache write.

I attached a short security-eval-checklist.pdf that outlines the artifacts procurement will request and estimates for lead times: hosted (1–2 weeks for EU pin + docs), dedicated (3–5 weeks), private/VPC (6–10+ weeks depending on connectivity).

Next step: can we lock a 30-minute technical slot on Thu 19 Mar 2026 09:00 CET / 17:00 SGT to do a network topology review? I'll include a short runbook and the KMS integration doc in that meeting invite.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Integrations | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference

Attachments: security-eval-checklist.pdf
